title: November 14 — SlimeBody: from gel and flow to a pumping, nutrient-carrying body
summary: SlimeBody closes a previously missing physical loop: local contractions determine elastic pressure and tube flow; upwind flow carries nutrient/signal; local food intake creates fluid and pressure, while flow supports adaptive veins and nutrient-funded growth. Its three-seed tests reveal that an imposed body-length wave moves tracer much farther than the self-organized rhythm, but equal amplitude is not equal pumping work. The engine omits Taylor dispersion and does not establish autonomous optimization, maze solving, or a useful learned timing rule.

nodes.claim: A continuous spatial slime-mould-inspired body couples node contraction phases to elastic pressure, implicit graph flow, upwind nutrient/signal transport, flow-dependent tube upkeep, local food-to-fluid conversion and front growth.
nodes.survived: The README and tests report a pressure/transport engine rather than decorative moving trails. In three frozen-body gate-1 trials, an imposed body-length contraction wave transported a mean 12.7% of tracer nutrient past halfway, versus 0.02% for shuffled phases and 0.9% for the body's own rhythm. The three-seed living-world layer audit reports 4,536 end nodes for the full model versus 713 without pumping.
nodes.killed: Transport does not implement Taylor dispersion; parcels mix at well-mixed nodes. Gate 1 matches contraction amplitude but not pump work (shuffled waves do 20–25 times less work), so the large delivery gap is not an energy-matched efficiency advantage. The body self-organizes poor long-range waves, the food-signal ablation is effectively null, tube adaptation does not improve food acquisition in the tested world, the near-gap-only path result is chemotaxis rather than maze solving, and history/reconnection/tempo tests remain unmeasured.
nodes.era: November 14: living material learns to pump

edges.why: SlimeBody's README explicitly credits the Physarum/Tero conductance and flux-adaptation ideas from Limasieni; its hydraulic body is new code, not imported Limasieni code.
SlimeBody explicitly credits the vine/economy line for maintenance, pruning and nutrient refund. This records conceptual transfer rather than reused source code.
SlimeBody explicitly credits GelatinIsland's spatial growing front but replaces the excitable medium with hydraulics, nutrients and phase-coupled contractions.

motifs.title: A useful imposed wave is not a self-discovered pumping strategy
motifs.description: The same built hydraulic body transports an end-loaded tracer under externally imposed body-length contractions, but its native phase field transports much less. This motivates an equal-work comparison and a test of whether local nutrient/contraction feedback can discover long-range coordinated pumping without an external phase target.

motifs.title: A layer can sustain a body without improving food finding
motifs.description: SlimeBody's layer audit separates chemotactic discovery (strongly smell-dependent) from hydraulic support of a grown body (pumping-dependent); tube adaptation can make anatomy look physiological without improving food acquisition in the current meadow. This is a functional dissociation, not proof of learned self-maintaining intelligence.
